$comment: CS-52. Every executable check in this repository, classified, with the
reason. `npm run checks:registry` verifies each classification against what
.github/workflows actually executes, so an entry cannot drift into being
decorative: a check recorded as operator-only that CI quietly starts running
fails here, and so does one recorded as ci that nothing runs.
Read `operator-only` as the explicit statement it is: the existence of that
file is NOT evidence that the thing it checks has been verified. Somebody
has to run it against the live host and record the result.

classifications.ci: Executed on every push and pull request. Its result is evidence about the commit.
classifications.deploy: Executed during deployment against the live host. Evidence about production, not about the commit.
classifications.on-demand: Executed by CI infrastructure only when dispatched. Evidence exists only for runs someone triggered.
classifications.operator-only: Requires a live deployed host. Existence is NOT evidence; only a recorded run is.
classifications.manual: A developer tool needing arguments, a local baseline or hardware CI does not have.

checks.reason: Starts and tears down its own disposable Postgres container, so pg_dump/pg_restore is genuinely exercised on a GitHub runner.
Re-executes itself in a container whose object directory is a 2MB tmpfs, so the filesystem genuinely exhausts. Needs only Docker and the built CareerScope core, both of which a runner has.
Asserts fourteen properties of the live host's nftables ruleset. There is no ruleset on a runner, so its existence proves nothing about the firewall.
Drives a real account through the deployed origin over real TLS and needs registration temporarily enabled. Cannot run unattended, and never in CI.
Probes the deployed origin's behaviour and headers. Only meaningful against careerscope.tech, so a green repository says nothing about it.
Verifies the holding page and its lift on the live proxy. Requires the deployed Caddy instance; nothing in CI can stand in for it.
Self-contained against stub docker and curl binaries, needing no real host, container or webhook (CS-24).
Authenticates the real owner against the deployed origin. It touches owner credentials and must never run unattended in CI.
Proves the running containers, the shipped tree and the recorded revision all agree. deploy.yml runs it over ssh after shipping; it is evidence about production, not about the commit.
Self-contained against stub curl and restart-stack.sh binaries, so the recovery logic is exercised without a proxy (CS-3).
Reads EXPLAIN output from the production database, whose plans depend on real data volume and statistics. A runner's empty database would produce plans that prove nothing.
Inspects the deployed queue's live state. The runtime half of the same contract is covered in CI by scripts/check-queue-runtime.ts.
Brings up compose.acceptance.yml with --no-build, so it requires production images already built locally. CI builds no such images, and building them here would duplicate the deploy path.
Self-contained against stub systemctl, systemd-analyze and curl binaries. It exists mainly to keep proving its negative cases (CS-47).
Verifies certificate issuance and renewal behaviour, which depends on the live domain, its DNS and the ACME account. No runner can reproduce that.
Drives the encrypted admin snapshot in a browser against local fixtures; runs in the verify job after the Pages build.
Static validation of the agent roster and its permissions. Runs through gates:test in the verify job.
Proves the agile gates still refuse malformed and blocked state. Runs through gates:test.
Requests the deployed API's routes at https://careerscope.tech and asserts their status and exposure. It is a probe of production, not of the commit.
This check. It must itself run on every push, or the classification it enforces becomes the next thing nobody executes.
Probes SQLite durability inside a prebuilt careerscope:local image. The obsolete container line is not deployed, and CI's opt-in image job builds a different tag.
Static validation of the repository's prompts, instructions and skills. Needs nothing but the working tree, so there is no reason for it not to run on every push.
Proves the deploy gate still refuses. Runs through gates:test — a gate nobody exercises is a gate nobody knows is broken.
Static check over the working tree, run through gates:test.
Compares the committed Pages screenshots in scripts/pages-baseline on every push and pull request, so visual regressions are release evidence rather than a developer-only check.

Runs first in gates:test. The repository declares Node >=24 in six places and a whole night of local verification ran on v22.23.2 regardless; only one test noticed, by accident, because Node 22 rejects a flag the runner passes. A floor enforced by accident is not a floor.

Asks mechanically whether any acceptance criterion is contradicted by the ticket's own record or by the limitations register. Advisory for ticket findings; hard-fails on unreadable input or an empty UAT selection. Four confirmed demotions were all caught by this one question.
Validates the recorded engineering progress state. Runs through gates:test.
Verifies the public Pages workspace artifact in the verify job, after staging.
Proves the release gate still refuses a release it cannot substantiate. Runs through gates:test.
Static validation of project-local skills: frontmatter, naming, provenance and absence of machine-specific paths. Needs only the working tree.
Proves the state readers refuse corrupt input instead of reporting an empty result. Runs through gates:test.
CS-68's guard over root-workspace test files. It has to run on every push, or the two files it just rescued could drift out of CI again unnoticed.
Validates ticket ownership, architecture disclosures and displayed status metadata on every push so the engineering board cannot silently contradict its evidence.
The browser acceptance suite, run in the verify job against the built app.
Measures a local inference server's throughput. No runner has one, AI is off by policy, and a benchmark asserts nothing a CI pass could rely on.
Kills real child processes between a durable write and its visible effect, then proves the survivor reconciles. Needs Postgres, LocalStack and a filesystem — all obtainable on a runner (CS-52).

Dumps a live Postgres and restores it into a fresh disposable container, comparing per-table fingerprints. Needs a Docker-controlled source container, which is why the recovery job starts Postgres itself rather than using a service container (CS-52).

Not a check but a scheduled job, invoked by careerscope-liveness.timer on the host; it re-verifies saved leads against the real internet. Its logic is covered in CI by check-lead-liveness.test.ts in test:integration.

Asserts hard p95/p99 ceilings. A shared runner's variance would make those flake, and the only ways to make a flaky ceiling green are to inflate it or retry — both forbidden. Dispatched deliberately instead, so a failure means a regression.
Restarts an isolated Redis, restores from AOF and drives a real publisher and worker process lifecycle. It starts its own Redis container, so it needs only Docker and Postgres (CS-52).
Sustained mixed load, thirty minutes by default. Too long for every push, and shortening it until it fitted would stop it being a soak.

Type-checks the 15 v2 test files that `tsc -b` never saw, because the package builds exclude test files so they never reach dist. Asserts the resolved file count first: a tsconfig that includes nothing type-checks perfectly.
CS-52's structural half for the canonical workspace: every canonical test file must be claimed by an npm script. Runs early in the verify job.
browser acceptance and the axe-core accessibility baseline, run in the integration job against a production build (CS-15).
A tool, not a check: it takes a name, a URL and a reference PNG as arguments and reports a percentage. No reference images are committed, and it has no pass threshold to enforce.
